[$\{\text{questions industry cares about}\} \cap \{\text{academic expertise needed to solve them}\} \neq \emptyset$ !]{.takeaway-close}

::: {.notes}
Three questions about one checkout page.  Speed versus accuracy: the speed–regret frontier is classical Bayes sequential analysis; what is open is how far a small menu of tests falls short of it, for the priors, clocks, and contracts platforms actually have.  How many hypotheses: one formulation gives each idea a size or none, under one period's traffic; what is open is what a size is worth, learnt from the experiments that rule would itself have run.  Measuring the methods: randomisation protects the experiment we designed, but we analyse the one we logged.  What is open is whether the guarantee survives, whether the log can be certified, and whether a method can be scored at all.  Every "open" today meant "open as far as I know".  [click] The questions industry cares about, and those that need academic expertise to solve them, have a non-empty intersection.  Thank you.
:::
